title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Breast Cancer Screening: The ANIHTA Study
official: Introducing Artificial Intelligence in Personalised Breast Screening Programs: a Health Technology Assessment
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate how artificial intelligence (AI) can be integrated into an organized breast cancer screening program for women aged 50-74 years undergoing mammography screening.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can an AI-based workflow that identifies selected mammograms for review by a third radiologist improve or maintain the cancer detection rate compared with the current AI-supported double-reading workflow?
* How would this AI-based workflow affect recall rates, biopsy referrals, false-positive results, interval cancers, radiologists' workload, and the number of cases requiring third-reader review?

Researchers will compare the currently used screening strategy, in which mammograms are independently read by two radiologists with AI support, with an alternative AI-based strategy reconstructed using a target trial emulation approach. In the alternative strategy, predefined AI score thresholds will be used to identify selected cases for an offline review by an independent third radiologist.

Participants will not be asked to undergo additional examinations or changes to their clinical care. Researchers will use routinely collected mammography screening data, AI scores, radiologists' readings, screening outcomes, and follow-up information. The alternative AI-based screening workflow will be evaluated retrospectively and will not affect participants' screening results or clinical management.

interventions.name: Discrete Choice Experiment on AI-Supported Breast Cancer Screening

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Retrospective breast screening cohort

* Women aged 50 to 74 years at the time of screening who underwent mammography within the organized breast cancer screening program of Azienda Sanitaria Locale Roma 2 during the predefined historical observation period.
* Mammography examinations must have digital images suitable for retrospective analysis with Lunit INSIGHT MMG.
* Linked outcome information required to determine study endpoints must be available.

Healthcare professional DCE cohort - Healthcare professionals aged 18 years or older who are involved directly or indirectly in the organized breast cancer screening program of Azienda Sanitaria Locale Roma 2, including radiologists, public health physicians, screening program coordinators, and other healthcare professionals involved in the organization, management, or evaluation of the screening pathway.

Exclusion Criteria:

Retrospective breast screening cohort

* Women younger than 50 years or older than 74 years at the time of screening.
* Mammography examinations lacking essential image data or outcome information required for AI re-analysis or endpoint classification.
* Mammography examinations that cannot be linked to clinical records or cancer registry data when such linkage is required for outcome ascertainment.

Healthcare professional DCE cohort

\- No additional exclusion criteria are specified in the study protocol.
